comment: Cross-language contract for rate resolution.
Rate resolution exists twice by necessity: the cost rollups run in
Rust (crates/claudepot-core/src/pricing/book.rs) and the Activities
dashboard aggregates client-side over rows it already holds
(src/costs.ts). Two implementations drift -- that is how costs.ts
came to report a session unpriced that the Rust path priced fine.
Both sides run these vectors:
- crates/claudepot-core/src/pricing/book.rs :: shared_vectors_match_this_implementation
- src/costs.test.ts :: 'shared rate-resolution vectors'
Vectors are resolved against the BUNDLED book (no observed rate
history), so they stay stable regardless of what a given machine
has scraped. Add a vector whenever you add a resolution rule.
Every model the bundled table prices must be named by at least one
'exact' vector (book.rs :: every_bundled_model_has_an_exact_vector),
which is what forces the hand-built book in costs.test.ts to grow
with the Rust table rather than silently lag it.
expect: 'exact' | 'family_estimate' | 'unpriced'
input_per_mtok, cache_read_per_mtok: asserted when present. Fable 5.1
differs from Fable 5 only in its cache-read rate, so a model whose
multipliers are unusual needs cache_read_per_mtok to be pinned at all.
